validated_results.title: Dairy Product Consumption and Prostate Cancer Risk in the United States.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study investigating dairy product consumption and incident prostate cancer risk in US men.

extraction.population: Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening trial cohort

sample_size.excerpt: There were 4134 confirmed prostate cancer cases out of the 49,472 men in the PLCO cohort between 1998 and 2013 during the average of 11.2 follow-up years.

cases.excerpt: Among 49,472 men, 4134 were diagnosed with prostate cancer during an average follow-up period of 11.2 years.

effect_size.excerpt: Total dairy products had no statistically significant association with prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96–1.15 for highest quartile compared with lowest quartile, P -trend = 0.48) ( Table 2 ). Similarly, there were no associations with low-fat dairy products (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 0.98–1.17, P -trend = 0.34) or regular-fat dairy products (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96–1.15, P -trend = 0.90).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Similarly, there were no associations with low-fat dairy products (HR = 1.07, 95% CI = 0.98–1.17, P -trend = 0.34) or regular-fat dairy products (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96–1.15, P -trend = 0.90).

p_value.excerpt: Total dairy products had no statistically significant association with prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96–1.15 for highest quartile compared with lowest quartile, P -trend = 0.48) ( Table 2 ).

comparison.excerpt: Total dairy products had no statistically significant association with prostate cancer risk (HR = 1.05, 95% CI = 0.96–1.15 for highest quartile compared with lowest quartile, P -trend = 0.48) ( Table 2 ).

design.excerpt: We prospectively investigated the associations between dairy product consumption and prostate cancer risk among men in the United States.

timing.excerpt: This is a prospective analysis of the PLCO, which is a two-armed, randomized trial of cancer screening intervention with no dietary intervention

continent.excerpt: We prospectively investigated the associations between dairy product consumption and prostate cancer risk among men in the United States.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: To assess dairy product intakes as well as other food item and nutrient intakes, we used a self-administered, validated, 36-page DHQ which evaluated the participants’ usual consumption frequency and portion size of 124 food and beverage items over the past 12 months
